issues.legal_issue: A judgment in a prior suit does not operate as res judicata against the State when the State was not a party to that suit.
material_facts: The municipal body had earlier brought a suit concerning the disputed land, and that suit was dismissed on a technical ground.
The State was not a party to the earlier suit.
The State later initiated public-premises eviction proceedings concerning the land.
issues.conclusion: The earlier suit did not bind the State and did not bar the later eviction proceedings.
issues.legal_principle: A judgment in a proceeding to which the State was not a party does not bind the State; the Court also noted that the earlier suit had been dismissed on a technical ground.

predicates.later_public_premises_eviction_proceedin: A public authority initiates a proceeding seeking eviction from premises.
predicates.prior_suit_concerned_same_property: An earlier suit concerned the same property as the later proceeding.
predicates.state_not_party_to_prior_suit: The State was not a party to the earlier suit.

issues.definition: When a public authority brings an eviction proceeding concerning property addressed in an earlier suit, the earlier suit does not bind the State if the State was not a party to it.

issues.legal_issue: Dismissal of an earlier proceeding for non-prosecution without a decision on the merits does not operate as res judicata in a later proceeding.
material_facts: The State was a party to an earlier proceeding concerning the disputed premises.
After the proceeding was converted to one under the applicable eviction law, it was dismissed for default, and an application to recall that dismissal was also dismissed for non-prosecution.
The earlier proceeding was not decided on the merits, and the State later initiated another eviction proceeding concerning the premises.
issues.conclusion: The dismissal for non-prosecution did not operate as res judicata and did not bar the later proceeding.
issues.legal_principle: Res judicata requires a matter to have been heard and finally decided. Pulavarthi Venkata Subba Rao v. Valluri Jagannadha Rao states this requirement; Ram Gobinda Dawan v. Bhaktabala distinguishes a decision after full contest from a decision without a hearing and final determination; and Sheodan Singh v. Daryan Kunwar distinguishes a preliminary dismissal of an appeal that leaves a merits decision of the trial court confirmed from a dismissal that is not based on a merits decision. The Court also referred to State of U.P. v. Civil Judge.

rule.if: later_eviction_proceeding and state_participated_in_prior_proceeding and prior_proceeding_dismissed_for_nonprosecution and no_merits_decision

predicates.later_eviction_proceeding: A public authority initiates an eviction proceeding after an earlier proceeding concerning the same premises.
predicates.state_participated_in_prior_proceeding: The State was a party to the earlier proceeding.
predicates.prior_proceeding_dismissed_for_nonprosec: The earlier proceeding was dismissed because it was not prosecuted.
predicates.no_merits_decision: The earlier proceeding did not result in a decision on the merits.

issues.definition: If the State participated in an earlier eviction proceeding that was dismissed for non-prosecution without a merits decision, that dismissal does not prevent a later eviction proceeding from being considered.

issues.legal_issue: The bar on bringing a fresh suit after dismissal for the plaintiff's default does not apply when the earlier proceeding was not dismissed in the circumstances specified by the relevant procedural rule.
material_facts: The earlier eviction proceeding was dismissed for default by the prescribed authority.
The proceeding was not dismissed because the plaintiff failed to appear when the defendant appeared, which is the circumstance addressed by Order IX Rule 8 of the Code of Civil Procedure.
The State later initiated a further eviction proceeding.
issues.conclusion: Order IX Rule 9 of the Code of Civil Procedure did not apply to bar the later proceeding.
issues.legal_principle: Order IX Rule 9 of the Code of Civil Procedure bars a fresh suit on the same cause of action when the earlier suit was wholly or partly dismissed under Order IX Rule 8, and permits an application to set that dismissal aside for sufficient cause. Because the earlier proceeding was not dismissed under Rule 8, the Court held Rule 9 inapplicable.

predicates.later_statutory_eviction_proceeding: A public authority initiates a statutory proceeding seeking eviction.
predicates.prior_proceeding_dismissed_for_default: An earlier proceeding was dismissed for default.
predicates.prior_dismissal_not_due_to_plaintiff_abs: The earlier proceeding was not dismissed because the plaintiff failed to appear when the defendant appeared.

issues.definition: The default-dismissal bar does not apply to a later statutory eviction proceeding when the earlier proceeding was not dismissed for the plaintiff's absence while the defendant appeared.
